research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from player talent and role counts
talent control in lineup-level influence measures
methodological_questions: Does lineup role coverage vary within team and remain separable from talent and role counts?
Does talent control adequately absorb lineup-level role effects?
What exposure, sample size, label-derivation and placebo risks affect lineup-level role analyses?

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality vs talent as predictor of series wins. Record states corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124; after talent control the adaptation term was not significant (per-series logistic adapt_diff_z p=0.2755; team-in-series cluster adapt p=0.2449), while talent remained significant (p=0.0213 per-series; p=0.0095 clustered). Sample n=55 series. Recorded failure mechanism: A_unanswerable, limited by confounding and small sample.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type. Descriptive lineup-cell PPP gaps for named initiators (e.g., Jokic vs MIN lineup PPP 0.814, n=59; Giannis forced PULL_UP vs preferred DRIVE gap -0.540). Used min-15 gate on 8 play types and opposing DEFENSE_LINEUP at ~84% coverage. Recorded: no placebo or matching; no validation recorded; later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

Sequence-memory lag effects with game-state controls. Lag-1 play-type effects present naively, lag-2 small, lag-3+ near zero. DRIVE and PNR lag-1 effects disappeared with game-state controls and within-team baseline (DRIVE ctrl_p=0.0911; PNR controlled p=0.136). Recorded failure mechanism: C_artifact. Sample size NOT_RECORDED.

Routing prior vs H2H posterior gate diagnostic. Mean PPP lead-vs-default delta of +1.26 at n>=5 and +1.13 at n>=15; recorded as small-sample inflation, with low-n leaders being role players with 2-3 PPP on 5-7 possessions. Recorded failure mechanism: C_artifact, limited by small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing a coaching/structural-adaptation measure as a predictor of outcomes after controlling for team talent
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: after talent control the adaptation term was not distinguishable from zero; ~55 series could not separate adaptation from roster quality, and talent and adaptation were correlated (+0.124).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Identifying lineup and forced-play-type suppressors for star initiators from descriptive cell PPP gaps
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE: no placebo or matching, no validation recorded, and later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Lag-1 play-type PPP effects in the possession sequence
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the naive effects disappeared under game-state controls and within-team baselines.
Recorded as C_artifact: small-sample inflation at n=5-15 (e.g., n=6, PPP=3.00) produced apparent edges.

evidence_establishes: Earlier studies in this project that used talent (net-rating) control and small team- or series-level samples found talent absorbed most apparent structural effects; the adaptation term was not separable from talent in n~55 series (FAM:SF-APPS-027).
Descriptive play-type and lineup-cell gaps in this project's possession graph were not robust under game-state controls, within-team baselines, or placebo checks (FAM:SF-CHT-037, FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Small-n cells (roughly n<15) produced inflated PPP effects in earlier work (FAM:SF31), so exposure thresholds are a known hazard.
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records studies organizer, shaper or terminal lineup coverage directly; no record defines these roles or reports within-team coverage variance.
No retrieved record reports the separability of lineup role coverage from talent or role counts.
Whether the 420,993-possession, 90 team-season data set has enough lineup-level exposure for the question is not established by any record.
The retrieved records are truncated (cut at 'read_family for the full text'); their full statistical detail was not read.
own_inferences: The question is stated as a joint condition (within-team variation, separability from talent and counts, and talent-control behaviour). It is only testable if each part has a pre-specified metric and threshold.
The earlier talent-versus-structure result (SF-APPS-027) suggests talent control may absorb most of the signal, so the separability component is the likeliest point of failure.
Role labels are probably derived from the graph's play-type and initiator records, so the labels are built from the same outcome-linked data used to measure influence (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL risk).
uncertainties: The operational definitions of organizer, shaper and terminal are not in the task or in any retrieved record.
Minimum lineup-stint exposure and cell thresholds are not specified.
Whether 2025-26 playoff data (complete from 2026-06-21) and regular-season data (complete from 2026-04-13) are both included is not specified; the question date 2026-07-13 implies both are complete.
Retrieved records were text-search matches on adjacent topics, not direct studies of the question; relevance is partial.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records indicate that talent-controlled structural effects were not separable in an earlier study (SF-APPS-027), that descriptive lineup and sequence gaps were artifacts under controls (SF-CHT-037, SF-CHT-009), and that small-n cells inflate effects (SF31). These records lead to proceeding only with pre-specified role definitions, exposure floors, placebo and negative-control tests, and a separability test that can fail. A plain proceed was therefore changed to proceed_with_changes.

blocking_constraints.text: Organizer/shaper/terminal labels, if derived from graph play-type and points records, share outcome information with the influence measure; labels must be defined from pre-outcome structure or validated against an independent source.
Lineup-level role coverage cells may be sparse; earlier work showed inflated effects at n<15 (FAM:SF31). A minimum-possession floor must be fixed before analysis.
Talent and role counts are correlated with coverage; FAM:SF-APPS-027 found talent absorbed the structural term, so separability is not assured.
Within-team coverage variance may be mostly noise across seasons; reliability must be estimated (split-half or cross-season) before interpreting variance.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record studies lineup role coverage (organizer, shaper, terminal) against talent or role counts. Related work found talent control absorbed a structural adaptation term (SF-APPS-027, untestable), descriptive star-lineup gaps lacked placebo checks (SF-CHT-009), sequence and routing effects were artifacts under controls or small-n (SF-CHT-037, SF31). The question is therefore not answered, though its methods are partly informed by these records.

risks.text: Role labels derived from outcome-linked play-type or points data may make coverage correlate with influence by construction.
Lineup-role cells with few possessions can produce inflated PPP (FAM:SF31).
Talent, minutes, game state and opponent lineup may drive both coverage and outcomes; FAM:SF-CHT-037 showed game-state controls removed apparent effects.
Descriptive star-lineup findings (FAM:SF-CHT-009) lacked placebo tests and were later treated as artifacts.
Within-team variance in coverage may not be stable across seasons, so separability may be unmeasurable.
With 90 team-seasons, within-team variance and talent-separation tests have limited power; FAM:SF-APPS-027 had only n=55 series.
Three roles, multiple thresholds and several controls create many comparisons.
Derived possession records from the graph database and play-by-play join may mis-assign players or possessions.

design.estimand: Within-team variance in lineup-level role coverage (organizer, shaper, terminal) and its partial association with lineup-level possession outcomes after talent (shrunk RS net-rating or RAPM) and role-count controls.
design.unit: Lineup-stint or team-season-lineup cell, with possession-level outcomes aggregated within cell.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons (all complete as of 2026-07-13); playoffs as a secondary sample only; 420,993 possessions, 90 team-seasons. Role definitions must be fixed and documented before any outcome is examined.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum possession floor per lineup cell (e.g., >=30 possessions) and a minimum number of cells per team-season; run a simulation to confirm power for the within-team variance and separability tests before analysis. If the floor leaves too few cells, report untestable rather than relax it.
design.controls: Talent (shrunk net rating or RAPM), role counts, minutes, period, clock, score margin, opposing lineup, season fixed effects, team fixed effects for the within-team comparison. Use within-team baselines as in FAM:SF-CHT-037.
design.falsification: Placebo role labels (shuffled play-type assignment within lineup) and a negative-control outcome (e.g., non-possession events) must show no effect; if placebo effects match real ones, the result is an artifact.
design.multiplicity: Holm correction across the three roles and pre-specified coverage thresholds.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) within-team coverage variance exceeds a permutation null, (b) coverage retains a partial association after talent and count controls surviving Holm correction, and (c) placebo labels and negative-control outcomes show no comparable effect. Otherwise report uncertain or artifact; report untestable if the exposure floor leaves insufficient cells.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular-season files complete as of 2026-07-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21. Exclude any partial pre-completion pulls.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)

- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
